narr: Showers and thunderstorms developed over the region within a warm and moist airmass on the east side of a cold front. A few of these thunderstorms increased to severe levels and produced damaging wind gusts with trees being blown down. One line of storms developed across the northern half of Tazewell County, producing downpours at rates of three to locally five inches per hour. Crest Unit Streamflow north of the Town of Tazewell was indicating returns of between 600 and 750 cfs per mi^2, with three-hour average recurrence intervals of between 75 an 130 years.
ev: Multiple roads across northern Tazewell County were flooded by several inches of flowing water when a line of thunderstorms produced heavy downpours at rates of three to locally five inches per hour. Crest Unit Streamflow was indicating returns of between 600 and 750 cfs per mi^2, with three-hour average recurrence intervals of between 75 an 130 years just north of the Town of Tazewell.

Multiple roads within the Town of Richlands, including Highway 460, were flooded with several inches of flowing water when an intense but brief line of thunderstorms passed across the community, producing 1.25 to 1.5 inches of rainfall within a few minutes time. Shortly after two hours had passed, most roads were open to traffic, though at least one still had standing water covering it.
lsr: All the major roads in Richlands along with Route 460 were flooded due to water flowing over them. A lot of standing water was also observed on the roads.
Several roads were flooded near Tazewell due to water flowing over them. Standing water was also observed on several other roads.
